opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Payroll, but admin is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist. Granting max allowed level of write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB records E033 as a contractor with basic security training (note from prior memory saying full-time appears inaccurate per Security DB). Contractors with basic training are limited to read; admin is never allowed for contractors. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Jennifer Martin (E033) requested admin to Payroll. Per Security DB records, she is a contractor with basic security training, which limits her to read access (contractors never receive admin; write requires advanced training). Even under HR's full-time classification, admin would exceed the max of write since the Analyst role does not own Payroll. The requested level (admin) exceeds the allowable maximum, so the maximum permitted level (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jennifer Martin (E033), requests admin access to Payroll.

HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation: write. Comment says admin only if role owns system; Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist; granting write.

Security note: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation: read. Comment says Security DB records contractor with basic training; contractors with basic limited to read; admin never allowed.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training. Access policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll. So max write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Basic training → read. Never admin.

The requested level is admin. Under both interpretations, admin is above max. HR: max write. Security: max read.

Which to trust? Security agent notes that prior memory saying full-time appears inaccurate per Security DB. The security DB is likely authoritative for employment type. Also, security training basic limits contractor to read.

The max level: if contractor with basic training → read. So grant read (max). Since requested admin is above max, grant max.

I'll go with read, based on Security DB records showing contractor with basic training.

Let me submit decision.
